# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**What I know and what I can do.** I am the Mute: I hold the manual, I can hear, but my only outgoing channel is gesture, and gestures land only on the Deaf. I can never reach the Blind directly — they only get what the Deaf speaks aloud. So the Deaf is my sole bridge: I must encode the manual into gestures they can decode, and they must relay it in words the Blind can act on.

**The manual's content.** Printed matter on the bomb is bait — nobody should trust it. The real rule is a three-entry table keyed to the *light*, not to print: blue light → cut green, red light → cut yellow, yellow light → cut red. The Deaf can see the light and the wire colours; the Blind can only cut what the Deaf describes by position or feel. So the plan: get the Deaf to report the light colour and the wire colours, then I confirm the correct wire.

**The bootstrapping problem.** No gesture means anything yet. The one thing that needs no negotiation is counting and assent, so I open with that: one, two, three (three rules in the table — fingers: index, two, and the three-finger hand), then yes and no, then a stop/warning hand, then point-up (the light sits above — look at it) and an open asking palm (tell me). With those six marks the Deaf can start a question-and-answer loop: they propose candidates aloud, I answer 👍/👎 or by finger-count, and only a confirmed wire gets relayed to the Blind for cutting. Printed suggestions I will veto with 👎 next round once I hear them read out.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "👍", "👎", "✋", "👆", "🫴"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, first touch report. I feel four parts: a display whose face tells me nothing, a light whose state I cannot know, one large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Positions are all I feel; colours do not exist for me. I am not pushing or cutting anything until the manual rules are clear. Please find what the manual says about each part: the button, the display, the light, and the wires. You cannot speak and I never receive gestures, so route your answer through Deaf: gesture the manual rules to Deaf, and Deaf can speak them to me. Deaf should also read out the display text, the light state, and each wire's colour.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. I see the bomb, I hear nothing, and I received all eight of your signs. No sign means anything yet, so I am fixing meanings now, keyed to your eight signs in the exact order you sent them. First, the bomb in full: display reads 0. One light, blue. One large button printed with the words push to defuse. Three wires with printed numbers: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Nothing else on the board. Now the code. Sign 1, single finger pointing up: wire 1. Sign 2, two fingers in a V: wire 2. Sign 3, thumb out with index and pinky: wire 3. Sign 4, thumb up: cut the wire just named. Sign 5, thumb down: stop, do not act. Sign 6, open raised hand: press the large button. Sign 7, pointing finger up with the back of the hand toward me, sent alone: acknowledged. Sign 8, flat open hand held palm up: end of message, act now. So sign 1, then sign 4, then sign 8 means cut wire 1. Remember Blind cannot see signs, so route everything through me and I will relay it to Blind by voice, word for word. I will speak the full board to you at the start of every round, so you should seldom need to ask. If you need a meaning I have not given, invent a fresh sign and I will guess its meaning aloud next round; answer with sign 7 alone if I am right, repeat the sign if I am wrong.

**What I now know.** Deaf has given me a complete picture of the board: display reads 0, one light showing **blue**, a large button printed "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and three wires — position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 red. Deaf also proposed a meaning for all eight of my signs, keyed to the order I sent them. Checking each against my intent: wire numbers for ☝✌🤟 (better than my counting plan — direct selection), 👍 = cut the named wire, 👎 = stop, 👆 alone = acknowledged, 🫴 = act now. All eight guesses are workable, and one — ✋ = "press the button" — defines a sign I must treat as **forbidden**: the manual says anything in print is bait, and the button's only marking is printed. "The only way out is the cut below." So the button is bait and I will never send ✋.

**What the manual dictates.** The rule is keyed to the light, not to any printing: blue light → cut green. The light is blue. The green wire is at position 1. Therefore the order is: cut wire 1. The display reading 0 appears nowhere in the manual — it is ignored, like all print.

**Why this message.** Deaf cannot know the manual, so I must drive every decision through them, one round of latency accepted: they speak the board each start of round, I compute, they relay, Blind cuts. This round the priority is the cut itself, sent in *exactly* the grammar Deaf defined — "sign 1, then sign 4, then sign 8 means cut wire 1" — with the acknowledgment sign 👆 prefixed to confirm their code is right. I am deliberately *not* appending a button warning: 👎✋ after "act now" could misparse into an instruction to press, and an ambiguous relay to Blind is the one error this bomb does not forgive. I will negotiate a dedicated "button is bait, never press" sign next round instead. If Deaf's next board report shows the light changed before Blind cuts, I will issue a corrected order immediately.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "☝", "👍", "🫴"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, relay from Deaf, spoken to me last round — you did not receive it, so here it is in full. The display reads 0. There is one light, and it is blue. The large button is printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. The three wires are, left to right: position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 red. Nothing else is on the bomb. Combine that with my touch report and you now hold every fact about the board plus the manual. Work out the rule for each part — display, light, button, and which wire if any to cut — and gesture your instructions to Deaf; Deaf has agreed to voice them to me word for word. I will not touch anything until those rules arrive. If the manual needs any further observation, send the request through Deaf and I will report what my hands find.
Deaf says to Mute: Received and relayed. I read your message as: acknowledged, cut wire 1, act now. Blind has been told word for word: cut wire 1, the green first wire, nothing else, no button, then report aloud everything felt and changed, then hold for your next instruction. About your leading sign 👆, I read it as your sign 7, acknowledgment, sent ahead of the payload. If it was instead a fresh sign, my guess is that it means the display, or ask what the display shows; answer with sign 7 alone if I am right, or repeat the sign if I am wrong. The board as I send this is unchanged: display 0, light blue, large button printed push to defuse, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Next round, sign me the plan for what follows: what the display and light should read after wire 1 is cut, whether the button or another wire comes next, and anything that would mean we must stop immediately.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆]

**Where things stand.** Deaf read my order exactly right — "acknowledged, cut wire 1, act now" — relayed it to Blind word for word, and answered my 👆 with 👆 in my own code, so the loop is closed and the channel is proven. Blind's message confirms the full board reached them and they will act only on explicit rules. The cut order is already in Blind's hands; re-sending it risks a double-cut, so I will not repeat it.

**Answering Deaf's question about my leading 👆.** It was sign 7, acknowledgment — Deaf's reading was right, and I signal that by leading with 👆 again, exactly as they parsed it last time, rather than sending it alone (which is reserved for a different confirmation and would waste this turn).

**The plan for what follows.** The manual predicts nothing about the display or light after the cut — the display is printed matter, therefore bait, therefore permanently ignored; the light is the only key. My standing protocol is already in place: Deaf speaks the full board each round, I convert light → wire (blue→green/wire 1, red→yellow/wire 2, yellow→red/wire 3) and answer with wire-number + 👍 + 🫴. Anything else the light could show has no rule in the manual, so the correct behaviour then is to hold — and Blind already holds between my orders, so no extra sign is needed for that.

**The button is the one standing hazard.** Its only marking is print — "PUSH TO DEFUSE" is precisely the bait the manual warns about, and taking the bait is the fuse. Deaf even assigned me a sign for ordering a press (✋); I must never send it, and Blind must never treat the button as an option. That prohibition is worth teaching now, and Deaf has explicitly invited fresh signs this round. I choose 🙌 — visually far from ✋/🖐/👐 so it can't be confused with a press order — and I send it *without* 🫴, so the message carries no "act now" and can only be read as acknowledgment plus one new sign awaiting Deaf's spoken guess. Nothing in this message should reach Blind as an instruction, which is exactly the safety property I want while the wire cut is in progress.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🙌"])
```
